nodes.label: Moles, molar mass and particle counts
nodes.norm_label: moles, molar mass and particle counts
nodes.definition: Converting among mass, moles and number of particles using molar mass and Avogadro's number, including counting atoms within a formula.

nodes.label: Mass spectra and isotopes
nodes.definition: Interpreting mass spectra of elements: identifying isotopes from mass-to-charge peaks and relating relative abundance to average atomic mass.

nodes.label: Percent composition and empirical formulas
nodes.definition: Determining the elemental composition of a pure substance: mass percent, empirical formula from masses or percentages, and molecular formula from empirical formula and molar mass.

nodes.label: Composition of mixtures
nodes.definition: Using measured masses or other quantitative data to determine the relative amounts of components in a mixture and to distinguish mixtures from pure substances.

nodes.label: Electron configurations and atomic structure
nodes.definition: Subatomic particles, isotopes and ion charge, and writing or interpreting ground-state electron configurations of atoms and ions using the Aufbau principle, Hund's rule and the Pauli principle.

nodes.label: Photoelectron spectroscopy (PES)
nodes.definition: Reading PES spectra: peak position as binding energy of a subshell, relative peak height as number of electrons, and connecting spectra to electron configuration and nuclear charge.

nodes.label: Coulomb's law and effective nuclear charge
nodes.norm_label: coulomb's law and effective nuclear charge
nodes.definition: Explaining atomic and ionic behavior through the electrostatic attraction between charges, which grows with charge magnitude and shrinks with distance, including shielding and effective nuclear charge.

nodes.label: Atomic and ionic radius
nodes.definition: Predicting and explaining the sizes of atoms and ions across periods and down groups, including isoelectronic ions and ions versus their parent atoms.

nodes.label: Ionization energy
nodes.definition: Trends in first ionization energy and the pattern of successive ionization energies, including using large jumps to identify valence electrons.

nodes.label: Electronegativity trends
nodes.definition: The tendency of an atom in a bond to attract shared electrons, its periodic trend, and its explanation from nuclear charge and distance.

nodes.label: Ion charges and ionic formulas
nodes.definition: Predicting common ion charges from valence electrons and periodic position, and writing charge-neutral ionic formulas.

nodes.label: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding
nodes.definition: Classifying bonds as ionic, polar covalent, nonpolar covalent or metallic from the elements involved and electronegativity difference, and predicting properties that follow.

nodes.label: Bond polarity and partial charges
nodes.definition: Using electronegativity difference to decide whether a bond is polar, the direction of its dipole, and which atom carries the partial negative charge.

nodes.label: Bond potential-energy curves
nodes.definition: Interpreting the potential energy of two atoms as a function of distance: equilibrium bond length at the energy minimum, bond energy as the well depth, and the attractive and repulsive forces that shape the curve.

nodes.label: Bond order, length and strength
nodes.definition: Relating the number of shared electron pairs between two atoms (including fractional bond orders from resonance) to bond length and bond strength.

nodes.label: Ionic solids and lattice attraction
nodes.definition: The structure of ionic solids as lattices of alternating cations and anions, and comparing the strength of lattice attraction from ion charge and ion size.

nodes.label: Metals and alloys
nodes.definition: The electron-sea model of metallic bonding, the conductivity, malleability and ductility it explains, and the structures and properties of substitutional and interstitial alloys.

nodes.label: Lewis structures
nodes.definition: Drawing or interpreting Lewis electron-dot diagrams: counting total valence electrons, placing bonding and lone pairs, multiple bonds, octet exceptions and polyatomic-ion charges.

nodes.label: Formal charge
nodes.definition: Calculating the formal charge on atoms in a Lewis structure and using formal charges to judge which of several structures best represents a species.

nodes.label: Resonance and delocalization
nodes.definition: Representing a species with two or more valid Lewis structures, understanding the real structure as a hybrid with delocalized electrons, and the resulting equal or fractional bond orders.

nodes.label: Electron-domain counting
nodes.definition: Counting the electron domains around a central atom, where each lone pair and each bond (single, double or triple) counts as one domain.

nodes.label: Molecular geometry (VSEPR)
nodes.definition: Predicting electron-domain geometry and molecular shape from the arrangement of bonding and lone-pair domains around a central atom.

nodes.label: Bond angles
nodes.definition: Predicting or comparing bond angles from electron-domain geometry, including the compression caused by lone pairs.

nodes.label: Orbital hybridization
nodes.definition: Assigning sp, sp2 or sp3 hybridization to an atom from its number of electron domains.

nodes.label: Sigma and pi bonds
nodes.definition: Counting sigma and pi bonds in single, double and triple bonds and explaining restricted rotation about double bonds.

nodes.label: Molecular polarity
nodes.definition: Deciding whether a molecule has a net dipole from its bond dipoles and three-dimensional shape.

nodes.label: London dispersion forces
nodes.definition: Attractions arising from temporary dipoles, whose strength increases with the number of electrons (polarizability) and with contact surface area.

nodes.label: Dipole-dipole attractions
nodes.definition: Attractions between the permanent dipoles of polar molecules.

nodes.label: Hydrogen bonding
nodes.definition: The strong dipole attraction between an H atom bonded to N, O or F and a lone pair on a nearby N, O or F atom.

nodes.label: Ion-dipole attractions
nodes.definition: Attractions between ions and polar molecules, such as the orientation of water molecules around dissolved ions.

nodes.label: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
nodes.definition: Using the relative strength of intermolecular forces to explain or rank boiling point, melting point, vapor pressure, viscosity, surface tension or enthalpy of vaporization, and distinguishing intermolecular from intramolecular forces.

nodes.label: Types of solids
nodes.definition: Classifying solids as ionic, molecular, metallic or covalent-network (and crystalline or amorphous) and relating the particles and forces in each to melting point, hardness and conductivity.

nodes.label: Particle model of solids, liquids and gases
nodes.norm_label: particle model of solids, liquids and gases
nodes.definition: Describing the arrangement, spacing and motion of particles in solids, liquids and gases, and recognizing phase changes as physical changes.

nodes.label: Ideal gas law
nodes.definition: Using PV = nRT and its proportionalities (Boyle, Charles, Avogadro) to calculate or predict gas quantities, including gas density and molar mass.

nodes.label: Partial pressures and mole fraction
nodes.definition: Dalton's law: the total pressure of a gas mixture is the sum of partial pressures, and each partial pressure equals mole fraction times total pressure.

nodes.label: Kinetic molecular theory
nodes.definition: Explaining gas behavior from particle motion: average kinetic energy proportional to absolute temperature, speed depending on molar mass, Maxwell-Boltzmann distributions, and pressure from collisions.

nodes.label: Deviations from ideal gas behavior
nodes.definition: Explaining when and why real gases deviate from ideal behavior, through intermolecular attractions at low temperature and particle volume at high pressure.

nodes.label: Molarity and solution preparation
nodes.definition: Calculating and using molar concentration (moles of solute per liter of solution), including preparing a solution of a target concentration.

nodes.label: Dilution
nodes.definition: Relating concentrations and volumes before and after adding solvent, since moles of solute are unchanged (M1V1 = M2V2).

nodes.label: Particle representations of solutions
nodes.definition: Drawing and interpreting particulate diagrams of solutions: dissociation of ionic solutes, strong versus weak electrolytes, relative concentrations, and solute-solvent orientation.

nodes.label: Chromatography and distillation
nodes.definition: Separating mixture components by differences in intermolecular attractions: paper or column chromatography (stationary versus mobile phase) and distillation by volatility.

nodes.label: Solubility and 'like dissolves like'
nodes.definition: Predicting and explaining solubility and miscibility from the relative strength of solute-solute, solvent-solvent and solute-solvent attractions.

nodes.label: Spectroscopy and molecular transitions
nodes.definition: Matching regions of the electromagnetic spectrum to the molecular changes they cause: microwave to rotation, infrared to vibration, and UV-visible to electronic transitions.

nodes.label: Photon energy, wavelength and frequency
nodes.definition: Using E = hν and c = λν to relate photon energy, frequency and wavelength, and connecting photon energy to energy-level differences.

nodes.label: Beer-Lambert law and spectrophotometry
nodes.definition: Using A = εbc and calibration curves to relate absorbance to concentration, choosing a wavelength, and evaluating spectrophotometry procedures.

nodes.label: Writing and balancing chemical equations
nodes.definition: Writing balanced chemical equations from descriptions or observations so that atoms are conserved, with correct formulas, coefficients and phases.

nodes.label: Net ionic equations
nodes.definition: Writing complete and net ionic equations by dissociating strong electrolytes and removing spectator ions, conserving atoms and charge.

nodes.label: Particle diagrams of reactions
nodes.definition: Using particle-level drawings of reactants and products that conserve atoms and are consistent with the balanced equation, including showing limiting and excess reactants.

nodes.label: Physical versus chemical change
nodes.definition: Distinguishing physical changes, in which particle identity is unchanged, from chemical changes, in which bonds rearrange to form new substances.

nodes.label: Reaction stoichiometry
nodes.definition: Using mole ratios from a balanced equation to relate amounts of reactants and products by mass, moles, solution volume or gas volume.

nodes.label: Limiting reactant and yield
nodes.definition: Identifying the limiting reactant, calculating theoretical yield and excess reactant remaining, and calculating percent yield.

nodes.label: Titration stoichiometry
nodes.definition: Using the volume of a standard solution needed to reach the equivalence point, together with the balanced equation, to find an unknown amount or concentration; includes equivalence point versus endpoint and buret reading.

nodes.label: Classifying reactions
nodes.definition: Recognizing acid-base, redox (including combustion) and precipitation reactions from equations or observations.

nodes.label: Oxidation numbers
nodes.definition: Assigning oxidation numbers to atoms and using changes in oxidation number to identify which species are oxidized and reduced and how many electrons transfer.

nodes.label: Precipitation reactions
nodes.definition: Predicting whether a precipitate forms when solutions are mixed, using the AP-specified solubility facts (all sodium, potassium, ammonium and nitrate salts are soluble) and given data.

nodes.label: Brønsted-Lowry acids, bases and conjugate pairs
nodes.norm_label: brønsted-lowry acids, bases and conjugate pairs
nodes.definition: Identifying proton donors and acceptors in a reaction, writing conjugate acid-base pairs, and recognizing amphiprotic species such as water.

nodes.label: Redox half-reactions and balancing
nodes.definition: Writing oxidation and reduction half-reactions, combining them so electrons cancel, and balancing atoms and charge in redox equations.

nodes.label: Reaction rates
nodes.definition: Defining and determining average and instantaneous rates from concentration-time data, and relating rates of reactant loss and product formation through stoichiometry.

nodes.label: Rate laws and reaction order
nodes.definition: Determining reaction orders, the overall order, the rate constant and its units from experimental data, typically initial rates, and predicting rate changes when concentrations change.

nodes.label: Integrated rate laws and half-life
nodes.definition: Using concentration-versus-time relationships for zero, first and second order reactions, linear plots ([A], ln[A], 1/[A] versus time), rate constants from slopes, and first-order half-life.

nodes.label: Elementary reactions and molecularity
nodes.definition: Recognizing that an elementary step's rate law follows directly from its molecularity (unimolecular, bimolecular), unlike an overall reaction.

nodes.label: Collision model and temperature effects
nodes.definition: Explaining rate changes through collision frequency, the fraction of collisions with energy at least Ea (Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution), and correct orientation.

nodes.label: Activation energy and energy profiles
nodes.definition: Reading single- and multi-step reaction energy profiles: activation energy, transition states, intermediates, forward and reverse barriers, the rate-limiting barrier, and overall ΔH.

nodes.label: Reaction mechanisms and intermediates
nodes.definition: Combining elementary steps into an overall equation, and identifying intermediates (formed then consumed) and catalysts (consumed then regenerated).

nodes.label: Mechanisms and rate laws
nodes.definition: Deriving the rate law predicted by a mechanism from its slow step, including fast pre-equilibrium steps that eliminate intermediates, and testing mechanisms against experimental rate laws.

nodes.label: Catalysis
nodes.definition: How catalysts increase rate by providing an alternative mechanism with lower activation energy while being regenerated and leaving ΔH and K unchanged.

nodes.label: Endothermic and exothermic processes
nodes.definition: Identifying processes as endothermic or exothermic from temperature observations, the sign of q or ΔH, or energy diagrams, keeping system and surroundings distinct.

nodes.label: Heat transfer and thermal equilibrium
nodes.definition: Heat flows from hotter to colder matter until thermal equilibrium; energy lost by one part equals energy gained by the other; temperature differs from thermal energy.

nodes.label: Calorimetry and specific heat
nodes.definition: Using q = mcΔT, heat capacity and calorimeter data to determine heat transferred or the enthalpy change of a process, and evaluating calorimetry procedures and errors.

nodes.label: Energy of phase changes
nodes.definition: Heat absorbed or released during melting, vaporization, freezing and condensation (q = nΔH), constant temperature during a phase change, and heating or cooling curves.

nodes.label: Enthalpy of reaction
nodes.definition: The enthalpy change of a reaction as written, its sign, and how it scales with the amount reacting in a thermochemical equation.

nodes.label: Bond enthalpies
nodes.definition: Estimating ΔH of a reaction as the energy of bonds broken minus the energy of bonds formed, and explaining energy changes as bond breaking (endothermic) and formation (exothermic).

nodes.label: Standard enthalpies of formation
nodes.definition: Calculating ΔH°rxn as the sum of ΔHf° of products minus reactants, with elements in their standard states assigned zero.

nodes.label: Hess's law
nodes.definition: Finding the enthalpy change of a target reaction by reversing, scaling and adding equations with known ΔH, because enthalpy is a state function.

nodes.label: Dynamic equilibrium
nodes.definition: Understanding equilibrium as equal forward and reverse rates with constant (not necessarily equal) concentrations, and representing it with graphs or particle diagrams.

nodes.label: Equilibrium constant expressions
nodes.definition: Writing Kc, Kp and Q expressions from balanced equations, with coefficients as exponents and pure solids and liquids omitted.

nodes.label: Reaction quotient Q versus K
nodes.definition: Calculating Q for a non-equilibrium mixture and comparing it with K to predict the direction a reaction proceeds.

nodes.label: Calculating K
nodes.definition: Calculating an equilibrium constant by substituting equilibrium concentrations or partial pressures, including those obtained from initial amounts and stoichiometry.

nodes.label: Magnitude of K
nodes.definition: Interpreting the size of K: K much greater than 1 favors products, much less than 1 favors reactants, and K says nothing about reaction speed.

nodes.label: Manipulating equilibrium constants
nodes.definition: Finding K for a modified reaction: reversing gives 1/K, multiplying coefficients by n gives K^n, and adding reactions multiplies their K values.

nodes.label: Equilibrium concentrations from ICE tables
nodes.definition: Setting up initial-change-equilibrium tables and solving for equilibrium amounts, including when the small-x approximation is justified.

nodes.label: Le Châtelier's principle
nodes.definition: Predicting how an equilibrium shifts after changes in concentration, volume or pressure, or temperature, and recognizing that only temperature changes K.

nodes.label: Solubility equilibria and Ksp
nodes.definition: Writing Ksp expressions, converting between Ksp and molar solubility using formula stoichiometry, comparing solubilities, and predicting precipitation with Q versus Ksp.

nodes.label: Common-ion effect
nodes.definition: The decrease in solubility of a salt when an ion it shares is already present in solution, predicted qualitatively by Le Châtelier and quantitatively with Ksp.

nodes.label: Strong versus weak acids and bases
nodes.norm_label: strong versus weak acids and bases
nodes.definition: Distinguishing strong acids and bases (complete ionization) from weak ones (partial ionization), and separating acid strength from acid concentration.

nodes.label: pH, pOH and Kw
nodes.definition: Calculating pH and pOH from [H3O+] and [OH-] using logarithms and Kw, including for strong acids and bases, and interpreting the logarithmic scale.

nodes.label: Weak acid and base equilibria (Ka, Kb)
nodes.norm_label: weak acid and base equilibria (ka, kb)
nodes.definition: Writing Ka and Kb expressions, calculating pH or K for weak acid and base solutions, percent ionization, and Ka·Kb = Kw for conjugates.

nodes.label: Acid-base reactions and mixtures
nodes.definition: Determining the products, major species and pH after mixing acids and bases, treating strong-reactant reactions as going to completion and handling the remaining excess or conjugate.

nodes.label: Acid-base titration curves
nodes.definition: Interpreting pH titration curves: equivalence-point pH, half-equivalence where pH = pKa, buffer regions, major species along the curve, and polyprotic steps.

nodes.label: Molecular structure and acid strength
nodes.definition: Explaining relative acid strength from bond polarity and strength, electronegativity of nearby atoms (oxyacids, inductive effects), and stabilization of the conjugate base by resonance or charge.

nodes.label: pH, pKa and predominant species
nodes.definition: Comparing pH with pKa to determine whether the protonated or deprotonated form predominates, including indicator color and selection.

nodes.label: Buffers
nodes.definition: Identifying buffer components (a weak conjugate acid-base pair) and explaining how they consume added strong acid or base to resist pH change.

nodes.label: Henderson-Hasselbalch equation
nodes.definition: Calculating buffer pH from pKa and the ratio of conjugate base to acid, or the ratio needed for a target pH, including after small additions.

nodes.label: Buffer capacity
nodes.definition: How much acid or base a buffer can absorb depends on the amounts of its components, and is distinct from the buffer's pH.

nodes.label: pH and solubility
nodes.definition: Qualitatively predicting how pH affects the solubility of salts with basic anions or hydroxides through acid-base reactions that shift the dissolution equilibrium.

nodes.label: Entropy
nodes.definition: Predicting and explaining the sign of ΔS from dispersal of matter and energy (phase, moles of gas, volume, temperature), and calculating ΔS° from standard molar entropies.

nodes.label: Gibbs free energy and favorability
nodes.definition: Using ΔG° = ΔH° - TΔS° and the signs of ΔH and ΔS to determine thermodynamic favorability and the temperature at which favorability changes.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic versus kinetic control
nodes.definition: Distinguishing whether a process is thermodynamically favored from how fast it occurs: favorable processes can be slow when activation energy is large.

nodes.label: Free energy and equilibrium
nodes.definition: Relating ΔG° to K (ΔG° = -RT ln K), recognizing ΔG = 0 at equilibrium, and connecting the sign of ΔG° to whether K is greater or less than 1.

nodes.label: Thermodynamics of dissolution
nodes.definition: Explaining whether a salt dissolves through the balance of lattice and hydration interactions (ΔH) and the entropy change (ΔS) of dissolving.

nodes.label: Coupled reactions
nodes.definition: Driving a thermodynamically unfavorable process by coupling it with a favorable one so the overall ΔG is negative.

nodes.label: Galvanic and electrolytic cells
nodes.definition: Identifying the anode (oxidation) and cathode (reduction), electron flow, salt-bridge ion migration and electrode changes in galvanic and electrolytic cells.

nodes.label: Cell potential and free energy
nodes.definition: Calculating standard cell potential from reduction potentials, relating a positive E°cell to favorability, and using ΔG° = -nFE°.

nodes.label: Cell potential under nonstandard conditions
nodes.definition: Qualitatively predicting how concentrations change cell voltage using Q, concentration cells, and why voltage falls to zero as the cell reaches equilibrium.

nodes.label: Electrolysis and Faraday's law
nodes.definition: Relating current, time, charge (Q = It), moles of electrons (Faraday constant) and the amount of substance deposited or produced in electrolysis.

nodes.label: Colligative properties and molality
nodes.definition: Freezing-point depression, boiling-point elevation, osmotic pressure and vapor-pressure lowering, and molality. Removed from the current AP Chemistry exam.

nodes.label: Nuclear chemistry
nodes.definition: Radioactive decay modes, nuclear equations and nuclear binding energy. Not assessed on the current AP Chemistry exam (first-order half-life math belongs to integrated-rate-laws).

nodes.label: Organic nomenclature and functional groups
nodes.definition: Naming organic compounds, identifying functional groups and isomers as a goal in itself. Not assessed on the current AP Chemistry exam.

nodes.label: Descriptive reaction prediction
nodes.definition: Recall-based prediction of products for named reaction classes (complex ions, decomposition of specific compounds, flame tests, qualitative analysis schemes) beyond the AP-specified solubility and reaction-type knowledge.
